static_traits.name: Zhang Jie
static_traits.family_status: Husband was a salesman, No children after marriage; husband passed away a year ago
static_traits.social_status: Social and support systems affected after husband's passing; a few friends to confide in, but not yet discussing cooking-related Anxiety with them
static_traits.medical_history: Denying prior psychotherapy and similar problems; no significant physical illness history
static_traits.language_features: Negative-leaning tone, cautious and skeptical; able to clearly express experiences and thoughts; negative automatic thoughts present (catastrophizing, all-or-nothing, overgeneralization); cooperation fair but tending to avoid trying; Anxiety intensifying when discussing cooking

basic_info.main_problem: I keep having negative thoughts related to cooking ability; these thoughts began a year ago after my husband passed away; I doubt my cooking skill and feel Anxiety and unbearable when cooking, thus tending to avoid, leading to affected eating habits and Daily life.
basic_info.core_demands: Cooking-related Anxiety and Self-doubt beginning to affect overall well-being, hoping for support and guidance.
growth_experiences: Husband passed away a year ago (Widowed); previously often cooked together with husband and did not feel pressure; after being Widowed, cooking alone, the meaning of cooking changed for her, social and support systems damaged, Loneliness and pressure rising, further triggering Anxiety and negative predictions about cooking.

core_beliefs: I will mess things up/I am not competent enough.
If I do not do well, I will disappoint important people.

special_situations.event: Each time Walking into the kitchen to cook
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not have enough time to cook, the result will definitely taste terrible.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reducing Anxiety through Avoids cooking, ordering takeout, Distracting with other activities
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This time will be terrible; I will definitely mess it up.

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot cook the meal well, it equals disappointing my husband and shows I cannot do it.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reducing or avoiding cooking, not daring to taste after finishing, directly discarding the finished product
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will disappoint him, this definitely will not succeed.

special_situations.event: Feels intense nervousness when trying to make a simple pasta
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Once I am very Anxious, the dish will become inedible.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Stopping result evaluation under Anxiety, directly discarding food to avoid the feeling of failure
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This will be hard to swallow; forget it.

special_situations.event: Recalls cooking with her husband in the past and compares it with currently cooking alone
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Without his companionship and support, my cooking now will not turn out well.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Lowering cooking frequency, relying more on takeout to avoid feeling Loneliness and failure
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Dishes made now basically will not turn out well.

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be supported and recognized in intimate relationships and daily life (such as cooking), maintaining emotional connection with significant others
core_conflict.fear: Fearing failure when facing cooking alone, 'disappointing' the late husband, and further intensifying Loneliness and Self-denial
defense_goal: Reducing failure and Sense of guilt through Avoids cooking and not evaluating actual results
Keeps distance from the kitchen and cooking to maintain a brief sense of safety and control

object_relations.self_representation: A solo cook who needs to prove oneself and is prone to failure
object_relations.object_representation: (Internalized) husband as an important evaluator and expecting other, needing me to do very well to not be 'let down'

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes reality testing, suggesting trying a simple dish to observe the actual outcome
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client tends to understand suggestions as situations 'that may prove I cannot do it', fearing being defined by failure (transference: projecting self-critical expectations onto others' suggestions)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Responding in a hesitant and reserved tone, emphasizing 'may not work/still will fail', to delay or politely decline trying; cautious sentence patterns, frequent hypotheticals (e.g., 'if... may...'), avoiding commitment to concrete actions.

manifestations: Cooking alone after being Widowed, the shared act of cooking turning into a Being alone activity
Social and support systems damaged, rarely discussing cooking Anxiety with friends
In the kitchen, more easily triggers worries about failure and 'letting down'
outcomes: Changed eating habits; daily routine affected
Rising Self-doubt and Sense of guilt

manifestations: The meaning of cooking together with her husband in the past has vanished, and cooking alone can hardly carry the original emotional value
Links cooking results with whether she has let her husband down, losing the self-nourishing meaning of the process
outcomes: Over-focusing on outcomes, negating process experience
Tending to discard food, not conducting reality testing

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Self-demand 'must do very well, otherwise I will have let him down'
Evaluates cooking results by rigid success-failure standards ('should / must' sentences)

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Pre-assuming failure and Self-denial before Entering the kitchen
Skeptical and cautious toward suggestions and exercises, worrying about 'failing again'
Tends to direct attention toward mistakes and risks rather than the present steps

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, corresponding to 'acceptance'.
manifestations: Not tasting actual results after finishing cooking, directly discarding
Avoiding present experience and testing by worrying about future failure

positive_force: Having Good cooking experience and interest in the past, with an activatable capability foundation
Still has a few friends as potential support
Able to clearly describe the problem and willing to try small-step experiments (though skeptical, willing to be open)
negative_force: Catastrophic predictions, Black-and-white thinking and overgeneralization and other negative cognitive patterns
Loneliness and Weakened support system after being Widowed, changed meaning of cooking
Avoids cooking and discarding food, lacking reality testing
Significant Self-doubt and Sense of guilt, excessive self-blame

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids cooking (including not tasting after finishing, directly discarding food)
antecedent: Entering the kitchen or Thinking about having to cook
Cooking alone, recalling cooking together with the husband in the past
Intense Anxiety and negative predictions arising during cooking
target_behavior.core_reason: Loneliness and missing emotional connection after being Widowed changed the meaning of cooking; to avoid 'disappointing the husband/proving one cannot do it', forming catastrophic and all-or-nothing predictions, thus using avoidance to fend off failure and guilt.
target_behavior.function: Escaping Anxiety and the feeling of failure, maintaining security and a sense of control short-term; avoiding facing self-evaluation and negative emotions.
target_behavior.consequence: Changed eating habits and Daily life affected; overall Decline in sense of well-being; maintaining and Reinforcing negative beliefs, reducing opportunities for reality testing.
